system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer review — Project Kestrel.** Based on the supplied extracts only; underlying DD documents and the full SPA remain to be checked. Buyer positions below are recommendations, not agreed terms.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A higher general cap, with separate protection for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recoverability; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible** basket. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; no thresholds for protected categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, recovering qualifying claims from the first dollar once crossed; the Seller’s structure strands meaningful losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notification within **18 months**; limitations presumptively apply to all Claims. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, separate longer periods for other categories, and preservation of timely notified claims. | **Counter at 24 months and reject universal application**; the Buyer needs adequate reporting cycles to identify latent problems. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share the general cap and time limit. | Standalone capacity, authority, ownership and unencumbered-title protection, without baskets or knowledge/disclosure erosion. | **Seek a 100% price cap and six-year contractual claim period**, with NSW execution and limitation mechanics checked; ownership risk should not exhaust a small general warranty allowance. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception supplied. | Express preservation of fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment claims, including appropriate attribution to Seller representatives, and non-excludable statutory rights. | **Carve these out across every relevant provision**, including caps, deadlines, disclosure, knowledge and remedy restrictions; blanket drafting must not shelter dishonest conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of indexed data-room material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the issue, against identified warranties, in a fixed accessible record. | **Reject blanket and deemed disclosure; require specific, adequately detailed disclosures and an archived index**; document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable from records. | No constructive or imputed knowledge bar; preferably no knowledge exclusion at all. | **Delete; fallback to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal leads only**, excluding specific indemnities and protected categories; discoverability is not actual awareness of a warranty breach. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, although no final consent or satisfaction evidence is supplied. | A Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring effective consent and fulfilment of clause 11.3 conditions, without unacceptable amendments or costs. | **Do not complete until consent and associated conditions are verified**, with a long-stop termination right; approximately 30% of revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release after Completion. | Verified payout, repayment and effective release of all relevant security and guarantees at Completion, reflected in debt-free/cash-free mechanics. | **Require an agreed completion discharge mechanism and lender evidence, not a post-completion promise**; the Buyer must not inherit secured debt or pay for it twice. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional bonuses described as Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unclear. | Seller economic responsibility for completion-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. | **Quantify and expressly allocate through funds flow/price adjustment plus indemnity, without double counting**; describing them as Seller costs does not prevent the Company bearing payment liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity confined to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified cleared payment and effective ownership of relevant project materials, plus cover for ownership defects, third-party claims and remediation costs. | **Require completion evidence and a confirmatory assignment where needed, and broaden the standalone indemnity**; the issue is usable IP ownership, not merely the unpaid-fee amount. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational issue said not to be material; access, scope, notification duties and loss remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, containment, evidence preservation, legal assessment, updates and Seller-backed protection for pre-completion incident liabilities. | **Require an investigation/remediation covenant and specific indemnity, with completion protection if findings are material**; uncertainty neither proves a notifiable breach nor supports dismissing the risk. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course costs. | Aggregate assessment of timing, scope, enforceability, termination rights, accruals and ordinary-course status. | **Keep open pending DD-008/DD-011 review; apply consent controls and appropriate accounting treatment**; AUD 330,000 of related commitments cannot be classified solely by Seller assertion. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations presumptively apply to all Claims, including indemnities and other remedies. | An express matrix distinguishing general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, price adjustments and fraud. | **Redraft definitions, exclusions and precedence provisions together**; targeted protections are ineffective if general boilerplate overrides them. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register relied on as evidence of 100% ownership. | Independent reconciliation of issued capital and ownership, review of encumbrances, options and transfer restrictions, and effective transfer/registration deliverables. | **Verify the register against supporting corporate records and appropriate searches; retain robust title warranties**; the register alone does not establish an unencumbered, fully diluted 100% acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP considered settled under the general regime. | A separate pre-completion tax indemnity and suitable tax warranties, generally surviving seven years with assessment-period extensions; robust IP warranties and tailored protection for identified defects. | **Expressly reserve both categories and negotiate their scope, caps and survival separately**; Seller’s declaration of settlement does not resolve long-tail tax or core-IP exposure. |

**Completion priorities:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, bonus allocation, Ironquay ownership evidence and title verification. Keep the incident and renewals open pending evidence. Do not manufacture consent requirements: the supplied lease disclosure identifies **notification**, while Mossvale’s **assignment restriction** does not itself establish a share-sale consent requirement.
=== END ADVICE ===
